steps.content: [Message]
[Chat Message]

Otriana
Office - Break Room
Clutching her coffee cup in the break room, Tracy let out a groan of despair.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Then what have I been drinking three times a day? Roachaccino?!
She turns to trudge back to her desk, only to freeze at the sound of a feeble, ghostly voice behind her.
<size=30>Tracy? Traaaacy...</size>

Is she hallucinating from all this overtime? Has heaven finally come to headhunt her? Tracy turns around. There, in the shadowy corner of the break room, a forlorn spirit is beckoning her over with a wave.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Hey, over here!

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Oh hey, Evie? What brings you to the contractor team? Something you need taken care of?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Not exactly. I heard a few people haven't clocked in for days, and now no one can reach them. All their work got dumped on the contractors. I know you guys are under a ton of pressure right now. I didn't want to pile on.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I was just a bit worried. You haven't been using any stickers when we chat lately. Figured you might be swamped. So I wanted to stop by and check on you.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: If only everyone at Otriana were as thoughtful as you...
Tracy offers a hollow smile and lifts her phone screen like a piece of evidence, the 999+ unread work messages glowing damningly upon it.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: You're always the one checking in on me. My turn, right?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: So, my team's been on this Eastian culture deep-dive for our new makeup line, and I came across this saying: "sending charcoal in the snow." Basically means showing up when someone really needs it!
Evie produces a paper bag from behind her back.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: You didn't!!!! Moonbucks? Vanilla oat milk latte with extra sugar?! Oh—
Tracy receives it like a sacred offering, cradles it in both hands, and downs a long, grateful gulp.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Any life coming back?

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Yeah... a little.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Sigh... Looks like these personnel issues really hit you guys hard.

No clear explanation has ever come from the company or the Public Security Bureau about those vanished employees. And really, what does it matter? Workhorses like them are only meant to quietly absorb the extra workload. They're not entitled to ask questions.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: So what do you do? When work gets like this, I mean.
Tracy mumbles the question between sips.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Me? I mean... I don't know if my thing would work for you. But if you really want to know... you have to swear you won't tell anyone.
After a quick glance left and right, Evie leans in and drops her voice to a whisper...

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: What's with her...? It's like she's been waiting forever for someone to finally ask that. Wait, no. This is Evie we're talking about. My gold standard for a top-tier professional woman. Intellectual, poised, mature, warm. The human embodiment of grace under pressure...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: So, on weekends, I would...

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: You would...

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Go full fangirl mode!!
[Workstation]
Tracy has barely made it back from the break room, not yet seated, when her computer erupts in a series of urgent chimes.
Probably more grunt work—messy, exhausting, and needed yesterday—she figures, clicking open the message window. But it's not work at all. It's from a group chat called "Family Forever."
[Chat Message 8]

Smiling, Tracy types out the words "set the world on fire." But her gaze catches the B+ on the performance review resting near her hand. She pauses, reconsidering, and backspaces until the chat box is empty again.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Tracy. Good, you're here. Nelson's gone MIA too. His workload's yours now. Get his files sorted and take them over.
Just a moment ago, she was happily bouncing back with her coffee; now, all the air goes out of her.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Okay...
The words drag out of her, flat and heavy. She trudges over to Nelson's desk, lowers herself into his chair, and clicks open his desktop.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Let's see what we've got. Spreadsheets, proposals, deck... wait. What's that?

There, dead center on the desktop, is a video file Tracy doesn't recognize. The thumbnail freezes on a blonde girl bathed in gentle backlight, the corner of her mouth lifting into a smile aimed directly at Tracy...
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Wait, you? Fangirl mode?! Who's the idol? Guy or girl? Disian? Actor? Singer? Do I know them?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Shh, not so loud. I don't want to broadcast this to the whole office.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: I get it, I get it. Someone sees you have a life outside of spreadsheets, suddenly you're "not committed enough." Come on, you and me? Don't worry. My lips are sealed.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Honestly, she's just some underground idol. Super niche. You've probably never heard of her. But I figured... maybe you need something like that too. Something outside of work, that you actually like. Just a little thing to help you get through weeks like this, you know?

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Something I actually like? I don't think I have anything like that... Besides work, I just scroll on my phone. That's pretty much my life. But if I had to pick... then I guess I like someone like you, Evie. An angel who brings me Moonbucks.
Tracy looked up at the clock, and just like that, her smile collapsed into a cry of despair.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Ugh, back to my desk... That place is literally hell! When is an angel gonna descend and save me from that nightmare?
[Workstation]

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Still at Nelson's desk? How long does it take to sort a few files? Anyway, listen, I need all his projects wrapped up and on my desk by Friday. ...Hello? Tracy. You with me?

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Angel... I just saw an angel. Oh—sorry, boss!

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Almost done here. Just a lot of stuff to go through. Friday. Yeah, Friday's totally fine!
Once her boss leaves, satisfied, Tracy finally settles down and glances at the clock on the screen. She realizes she's just spent a full half hour staring blankly at that video thumbnail.

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Phanuel... Phanuel?

The name from the video title slips from her lips in an unconscious murmur. As if guided by some unseen force, her hands drag the file into her transfer list, nestling it among the ordinary work documents.

At the same time, a strange, exquisite pleasure washes over her. The world before her eyes takes on a fluffy, golden fringe. She feels blissfully adrift, as though suspended in pink clouds, her limbs entirely weightless.
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: She's taken over every screen, every speaker, every playlist in this city, and she's not slowing down! Phanuel is rewriting the rulebook on what an idol can be. So what's next for the girl who turned Eastside pink? Let's find out! Are you ready?

In the Bureau's Recreation Area, the TV screen is tuned to the Eastside entertainment channel, running a pre-concert promo. Phanuel's colossal posters dominate the frame, plastered across every wall of Eastside's central commercial strip.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: ...Another one of those online celebrities, huh?
Tucked into the corner of the couch, Joan keeps her head down, absorbed in tuning an old guitar. Every so often, she glances up at the screen.

The guitar bears its history in every nick and dent along its edges, its pickguard layered with band stickers bleached pale by time. She gives the pegs a few careful turns, plucks a couple of notes, and frowns. Something still isn't right.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: I hope this song brings a little happiness to everyone who's supported me!
[Play Song]

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: God, my ears are hurting... Is this what idols are putting out these days? This "arrangement" is just noise. I was writing better hooks in my sleep.
Joan's brow furrows. She pauses mid-tuning and reaches over for the remote. That's when the pre-chorus drums hit.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Wait...
[Theme Song Volume Increases]
Joan knows this melody by heart, so well that the next phrase arrives in her head before the singer on screen even opens her mouth. She holds up her guitar.
Mi re mi re mi re mi re mi mi mi sol mi...
The notes from her guitar and the audio from the TV land in perfect, coincidental sync.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: You're kidding me! This is a song from my old band's album!
She keeps playing, disbelief written all over her face. One phrase, then another, then another...

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: This is straight-up copy-paste! Who steals a song and doesn't even bother to change a note?!
She pulls the TV screen around to face her, and there it is: the smile that haunts every corner of the city, now gazing directly at her.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: What do you think? Thirty seconds isn't enough, right? Don't worry, the full version drops in three days, live at Phanuel's solo concert! Fan support events are already popping up all over the city—
Over and over, the TV repeats the melody she knows inside and out, accompanied by the gleaming tagline: "A fresh original, tailor-made for Phanuel." Joan sends the remote flying at the screen.
[Throws Remote, Black Screen Transition, Office Area]

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: I've checked for you. Chief is currently out of the Bureau. If this involves a dispute with an external entertainment company, you'll need to go through legal assistance.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: If you require legal help, please submit the relevant documentation first. We'll respond within five to seven business days.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Five to seven business days? Are you ****ing serious right now? Someone's about to steal my song and perform it at a concert in three days!

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: I understand your frustration, but... right now we simply don't have the resources to handle this volume of personal requests from Sinners. However... if this is really urgent, we can look into speeding things up.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Right. By the time you "speed things up," she'll have toured all of Eastside! My work. Stolen. Monetized. Fans getting ripped off, ears getting polluted, and you're just going to brush it off as a "personal request"?
Joan remains glued to the service window, refusing to move. She fails to notice the presence behind her until the girl in the sheriff's uniform delivers a sharp elbow, pushing Joan to the back.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: You're wasting your breath. Badgering the staff won't get you anywhere. Excuse me, are you done with her? I need my Corruptor extermination payout processed.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Huh? Oh... yes, of course!
A relieved breath escapes the staff member. Her hand reaches for Jane's report, only for a palm to come crashing down onto the counter with a sharp smack.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: You want to explain what that was about?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: ...A reality check. Eastside's got multiple Hollow Syndrome cases still open. Even field teams and intel have been pulled to assist the city arrest team. Nobody's sitting around with free time to care about a song.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Wow. "Reality." So I just sit back while they gut my music, repackage it as some bubblegum pop single, and toss me a few coins? Maybe a nice little collab email? Ha. Real gracious of the system. Should I send Phanuel a thank-you basket while I'm at it?

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: ...Ms. Jane, the base payment for your assistance on this task... has been processed... whenever you're ready to confirm...
Caught in the crossfire, the staff member speaks in a whisper so faint it could barely rouse a mosquito, terrified of sparking an explosion. Thankfully, both Jane and Joan let it drop.
Jane turns her attention to the payment check, done with the argument. But Joan, watching Jane's continued silence, lets out a cold, sharp laugh.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Yeah. Stick to Eastside. It suits you. Grind out your paychecks and keep your head down where the air smells like money and nothing else.
Joan heads off, guitar strapped to her back. Jane slips the signed form through the window, her gaze following Joan's silhouette until it reaches the end of the corridor.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I'd strongly suggest you don't do anything stupid, Ms. Joan.
Joan offers no reply. She walks out of the office area and heads directly for the A-Class Sinner detention area.
[In Front of a Detention Cell]

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Hey. I got a job for you.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: A big one. The kind that'll make everyone in Eastside remember your name.
[Crime Scene]

May 28, N.F. 116. A male resident of Eastside collapses without warning during his morning commute. No external trigger is identified. He loses consciousness. His face displays an abnormal, fixed smile. Following admission, his vital signs have stabilized, but he retains no memory of the event.
June 15, N.F. 116. A secondary school student loses consciousness without warning during a class break. The facial expression is identical to the first case.
June 28, N.F. 116. The third and fourth cases occur on the same day, at an Eastside commercial plaza and a community park, respectively. The onset pattern is consistent with previous cases.

Additional cases are reported. Victims are predominantly aged 12 to 25. Neither Banyan Hospital's Department of Neurology nor the Public Security Bureau's Criminal Investigation Department has identified any physiological, toxicological, or trauma-related cause. On July 3, N.F. 116, the case is officially transferred to the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control for centralized handling.
July 8, N.F. 116, A Youth Apartment in Eastside

By the time Wynn reaches the new crime scene, Eugene's team has already wrapped up the initial handover with the Public Security Bureau. Takeout bags have overtaken the apartment, spilling from the entryway into the living room, where they mingle with clothes and delivery boxes. Hardly an inch of floor is visible.
The victim, Nelson, had been absent from work for several consecutive days. According to the Bureau's preliminary assessment, he was lying unconscious for two full days without anyone knowing.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Victim's already been transported. His M-value was right at the threshold when we found him, highest possible before full corruption. Vitals are holding, but mentally... not optimistic.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Same as the previous cases. Unconscious, but with that weird, happy smile.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: People are calling it "Hollow Syndrome" online now. We're managing it, but without progress on the investigation, people are going to start asking questions we can't answer.

Both the Public Security Bureau and the MBCC are working together to keep a lid on public concern over the Hollow Syndrome. With DisCity already besieged by internal and external threats, even the faintest rumor of Mania activity in Eastside could spark an unnecessary panic. Unfortunately, the investigation isn't yielding promising results.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: These victims share no common threads. Different jobs. Different social circles. Different neighborhoods. Nothing links these people. As for the one thing they share, though, we haven't found any concrete evidence...
Eugene's gaze settles on the only tidy spot in the room: the desk. Its surface has been taken over by an army of pink merchandise.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Phanuel. Eastside's hottest new star. These days, her face is plastered on just about every popular brand out there.
The first Hollow Syndrome case occurred during the victim's commute, as a giant roadside screen played one of Phanuel's cosmetics advertisements.

Every subsequent case has since been traced to locations within the coverage of Phanuel's pre-concert new-song promotions. And as the case count climbs, so does the percentage of victims who consider themselves among Phanuel's fans.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: With how hard they're pushing her right now, a couple of merch items in any young person's apartment isn't exactly a red flag. But...

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: This? This is a lot, even for a fan.
[Chief's portrait]
But more evidence means more to work with. I don't think the Hollow Syndrome and Phanuel crossing paths is random. The last time her name came up, BR-003 was getting hit.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: On-site M-value scans are clear. No anomalies. We've ruled out direct contact transmission for now. Working theory right now is some other vector for Mania spread. Eugene's going to box up the evidence and bring it back to the Bureau for a deeper look.
You flip through the report Wynn hands you, then give Schorl a quick glance at it too.

options: A new type of sorcery, maybe?
Could this be connected to the Underground?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Insufficient information to confirm. No subjects have exhibited full Mania corruption or transformed into Corruptors. No contamination residue has been detected at any site. If the source is a known enemy, their methodology has demonstrably evolved.

Looking back at the recent cases, both the spread and severity have been notably restrained, almost cautious. It's as if the perpetrator has switched to a completely different style. More calculated, somehow.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Which is unfortunate for us. No obvious anomalies means no clear grounds to act. If this gets classified as a non-Mania case, the Bureau loses any justification to intervene in Eastside's civilian life.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sounds like you'd rather we sit this one out.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: ...I'm only here to assist with your actions, not to offer judgments. But based on probability modeling, I'd advise holding off. Let the situation develop. We may capture more reliable leads once things become more visible.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And while we wait, more people in Eastside pay the price. The next victim could be a statistic you don't care about. Or it could be one of those little geniuses at the Institute.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: So your interest in this idol really does trace back to the Ring Research Institute.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Protecting the mental health of minors is a pretty basic adult responsibility.
Your eyes return to the file. The agency backing Phanuel is a name you don't recognize at all: <color=#fb9259>Mirrormoon Entertainment</color>.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: In the strictest sense, you don't yet qualify as an adult—
Smack. You give Schorl a slap.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wynn, you and Eugene handle the on-site work. I've talked to Nightingale. She'll be at the Bureau running support for your investigation. Keep me updated through the usual channel.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And don't worry about me. FAC assigned a squad to watch my back.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: You're going somewhere else, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Seems like a good time to go meet this big new star. On behalf of some friends.
[Small CG: Three Threads Converge] [Muffled MV Sound]

steps.speaker: Tracy
steps.content: Phanuel...?
Settled back at her workstation, Tracy's fingers move on their own, pulling up that same video again.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: God, her singing sucks.
From every screen, pink light pours out, weaving through the urban maze of streets and lanes, while the cheerful melody saturates every corner of the city.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Hi everyone! Phanuel here! This summer, I want to fill every moment with sparkle, just you and me! Ready to shine together?

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Sing along with me! ♪ Even if tomorrow is a mystery...
♪ All I all I ask is for you to be with me!
[MV plays for 15 seconds] Ba, ba ba ba... Ba, ba ba ba...
